findings.issue: The interface A37 publishes does not match the one its dependents A38 and A71 were written against. A38 calls computeAllocation, transitionOrder(orderId,'settled',{register_entry_ref, holding_ref, recon_run_id}), postOrderRefund, postEscrowRelease and expireUnfunded, and consumes an A37 event offer.hard_cap_reached. A37 exposes previewAllocation, settle(order_id,{register_entry_id, register_version_id, token_delivery}), computeRefundBatch/executeRefundBatch, no escrow release and no hard-cap event. Both nodes draft the orders.allocation.lock approval (A37 lockAllocation and A38 F2). Both own a refund-batch table with different reason vocabularies (scaled_back/excluded_at_mint against scale_back/excluded_recipient/revert). Both run a 5-business-day refund clock (orders.refund_sla and refund.pay). Both own the soft-cap, units-issued and tokens-delivered timeline rows (/me/orders/{id} and /me/orders/{id}/settlement). A71 already flags the double allocation path and the double refunds queue. Built as written, one lock can raise two approvals and one refund can be drafted and paid through two batches.
findings.fix: Freeze one A37 index.ts contract and make A38 and A71 use it. (1) One owner for the allocation-lock approval; recommended: A37's lockAllocation raises it and A38 F2 calls it. (2) One refund_batch table, owned by A37, with one reason enum; A38 calls computeRefundBatch/executeRefundBatch. (3) Add postEscrowRelease to A37 (and remove the 'never releases escrow' line), or move the escrow-release journal and A16's caller registration to A38. (4) Emit offer.hard_cap_reached. (5) One settle signature: delivery proven by TokenDeliveryProvider or by recon_run_id, decided and used in both notes. (6) One refund SLA clock. (7) One owner for the timeline. Record these as loops on A38 and A71.

findings.issue: The rule for an agent order above its cap contradicts itself and A12. The spec's own agent paragraph, A12 (a signed payload A$1 above per_action_cap returns 428) and product-map J22 ('above the amount limit it waits for the person's passkey') all say 428 CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED. The oracle rule, the node summary, the 'Agent above the mandate' challenge (A$5,989.80 against a A$5,000 per-action cap) and the pass criteria all require 403 G22_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. The hidden oracle would test the opposite of the specified behaviour.
findings.fix: State one rule and use it everywhere. Recommended: above per_action_cap with a valid signature, return 428 and create no order row, reservation or journal. Hard limits (daily cap exhausted, scope, vehicle, time window, IP, hold or kill switch) return 403 G22_* with zero rows. Rewrite the challenge: 25 units gives 428 and zero rows, then the person's passkey gives exactly one funded order. Add a separate daily-cap vector that returns G22_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. Update the node summary in the graph to match.

findings.issue: The data model collides with A04's schema ownership. A04 already defines order, allocation and allocation_line in packages/db/src/schema/orders.ts, and A06 seeds orders into them. A37 declares 'Drizzle tables in the packages/db slice this node owns': orders (plural) and allocations with a lines[] array, plus five new tables. A37 owns no packages/db path, so the builder will either duplicate the tables or edit A04's files.
findings.fix: Use A04's order, allocation and allocation_line tables, adding missing columns through a recorded A04.x loop. Put the new tables (order_state_history, order_quote, disclosure_acknowledgement, refund_batch, order_confirmation) in modules/orders/schema.ts and modules/orders/migrations, registered through A04's registerModuleSchema as A36 does. Remove 'packages/db slice this node owns' and map every field to its table.

findings.issue: J22 step 4 ('Token stops at once; open agent orders cancelled') is not specified. A60 defers the whole behaviour to A37's spec, but A37 does not consume agent.token.revoked, agent.mandate.revoked or A101's hold and kill-switch events, and never says what happens to open agent orders. D04's instant revoke has no tested effect on orders already placed.
findings.fix: Consume agent.token.revoked and agent.mandate.revoked (and the kill switch where it applies). On revoke, orders from that token in submitted (pending 428) or awaiting_funds become cancelled with reason agent_token_revoked, reflection_period orders become revoked, and funded orders stay as the person's orders and the person is notified. Expose the open-order list for A60's consequences card (for example GET /v1/me/orders?token_id=). Add a challenge where revoke races an order.

findings.issue: The G13 criterion for settle cannot be met. Requirements covered and the pass criteria say a settle never proceeds without an approved A14 request whose payload_sha256 equals the file hash. But settle(order_id,{register_entry_id, register_version_id, token_delivery}) takes no approval id and checks no approval, so the builder cannot implement the criterion and QA cannot fail a build that lacks it.
findings.fix: Choose one. (a) settle takes the approval_id of A38's allocation.mint 6E+Q request, checks it is approved and that payload_sha256 equals the current locked file's file_sha256, and refuses with ORD_FILE_HASH_MISMATCH otherwise. (b) Remove settle from the G13 criterion and say G13 for delivery is enforced in A38/A28. Either way, add a challenge vector.

findings.issue: The agent disclosure rule contradicts itself. Under G12, a superseded document version makes the order 'rejected', so an order row exists. Under standing consent, a superseded IM for an agent returns '428 with documents_required' and creates nothing. Reconfirm by mandate signature 'records new acknowledgements', but standing consent covers only the versions acknowledged when the mandate was created.
findings.fix: Define the agent path. When standing consent does not cover the current versions, return 428 with documents_required and create no order row; person orders are still rejected as written. An agent reconfirm needs standing consent that covers the new version (under orders.agent_standing_consent) or a 428 for the person's passkey. Add both cases to the challenges.

findings.issue: The placement gate set ignores the offering's regime. G04 is always evaluated and G05 (target market fit) is never mentioned, although the spec supports au_mis_retail (reflection period, J16) and INV-01 and J16 list G05 for retail. A retail order would be checked for wholesale status and not for TMD fit.
findings.fix: Take the quote, placement and allocation gate sets from A19's order set for the offering's regime: wholesale uses G01, G04, G06, G07, G11, G12, G21; retail (P2) uses G01, G05, G06, G07, G11, G12, G21. Add a challenge: a retail order outside the target market is rejected with G05, and wholesale orders are never asked G05.

findings.issue: The fund_at=confirm variant breaks the escrow Δ 0 rule and the close path. The Δ sum counts only funded, allocated and refund_pending orders, but in this variant money sits in escrow while the order is in reflection_period or revoked. 'reflection_period → awaiting_funds on close, followed by expiry' would expire an order that has already paid. The fee leg of a partial refund is also left implicit.
findings.fix: Count reflection_period and revoked orders that hold money in the Δ sum. At close, a paid reflection-period order goes reflection_period → awaiting_funds → funded and is never expired. State that the partial-refund fee leg is fee_cents_funded − mulBp(allocated_cents, fee_bps, half_up), taken from fee_payable_realx. Add this variant to the Δ boundary challenge.

findings.issue: The escrow read leaks data across tenants. GET /v1/offerings/{id}/escrow is open to sponsor users under offerings:read and returns escrow_account_level (the bank mirror and the sum of every offering's escrow), which reveals other sponsors' client money in the shared escrow trust account.
findings.fix: Sponsor principals and their agents get only the per-offering fields. escrow_account_level is returned only under the staff scopes treasury:read or orders:read. Add a principal-probe challenge that checks this.

findings.issue: Dependencies are missing for interfaces and criteria the spec uses. The pass criteria diff against A06's seed, the pass criteria require exactly one A104 MCP tool per operation, and the spec consumes A42's investor.frozen event. None of A06, A104 or A42 is an ancestor of A37, and none would create a cycle.
findings.fix: Add A06, A104 and A42 to A37's deps. Alternatively, move the A104 tool-count criterion to A104 and put the A42 event behind an interface with a local fake.

findings.issue: allocate.ts goes into packages/domain/src/orders/ 'through loop A02.1', but A02 does not own that folder, which is unowned. The precedent (A12 owns domain/src/agent-authority, A20 owns domain/src/recon) is for a node to own its own domain subfolder. The loop adds a needless sign-off on a core oracle file and makes the 'only owned paths changed' check ambiguous.
findings.fix: Add <workspace>\app\packages\domain\src\orders\ to A37's owned_paths in the graph and the note, and drop loop A02.1. Keep loop A03.1.

findings.issue: Staff read contracts that A71 relies on are missing: GET /v1/admin/orders/{id}, GET /v1/admin/refund-batches, GET /v1/offerings/{id}/reconfirmations, and allowed_actions[] on admin/orders rows. The ADM-12 refunds queue and order detail have no specified source.
findings.fix: Add these routes (cursor-paginated, with x-realx-scope, and sla_due_at and approval id on refund batches) plus allowed_actions[] for the caller, or record them as loops agreed with A71.

findings.issue: The design-fidelity strings differ from the prototype. The design renders '64% of 75%', G07 as '0.10% (cap 5%)' and Share of trust as '0.10%'. The spec uses '64 % of 75 %' and '0.1 % (cap 5 %)', and the challenge diffs these strings exactly.
findings.fix: Use the prototype's exact strings in the contract and the challenge, or say that A57 does the formatting and the contract test compares only bps and integers.

findings.issue: Eight wikilinks do not resolve (A17, A19, A36, A50, A51, A57, A71, A95). The links use titles containing ':' or '/', but the files on disk use '-'.
findings.fix: Have the generator emit [[<filename>|<title>]], or sanitise link targets the same way it sanitises filenames.
